title: Precision
description: A scrubber for a four-minute track, set alone on warm paper. Drag the playhead and it follows the finger one to one; slide the pointer away from the track while you drag and the scrub slows continuously, from full speed through half, quarter and eighth to a sixteenth. Nothing says so: the ruler darkens under a loupe whose marks swell and sprout seconds, half-seconds and then tenths, and the time readout grows a tenth digit when seconds reach the glass and a hundredth when tenths do. Come back to the track and the playhead eases back under the finger without a jump. Only a full-speed release keeps its momentum.
intent: From Rauno Freiberg's Adaptive precision (https://rauno.me/craft/adaptive-precision) and iOS scrubbing speeds: a time slider whose precision rises as the pointer moves away from the track, communicated by the material itself rather than a label.
